summaries.0: This is a Python library called mlx-guard that provides external runtime safety supervision for MLX workloads on Apple Silicon. It helps prevent runaway MLX runs from causing a paging storm by supervising from outside and writing a crash-resilient JSON report of what happened.
summaries.1: The mlx_guard library is used to monitor and limit the memory usage of a process running on macOS, providing a safety boundary against runaway MLX processes. It can be used in conjunction with MetalGuard, another project, to defend different rings and prevent the whole Mac from crashing.
summaries.2: MetalGuard is a tool that monitors workload health from within a process and cross-checks it with an OS-accounted number. It is designed to work in conjunction with mlx-guard, another tool that provides an outer layer of protection when the process itself can no longer be trusted.

summaries.24: The native supervisor launches a child process with a specific configuration, including a positive root PID and a new Unix process group, before executing the child. summaries.25: When the root command's process exits, the supervisor no longer treats it as an unexplained loss if other members of its owned group are still running. The supervisor will now terminate any background work that was left running by the command.
summaries.26: Checkpoint delivery uses a cooperative endpoint negotiated from a caller-supplied identity, which is confirmed as a positive, live member of the owned group. The identity is revalidated immediately before signalling, and a PID whose identity no longer matches is refused as an invalid checkpoint endpoint.
